thread.title: Facebook may be the ‘comeback story of 2019’ as stock soars higher

author: Emily Bary
title: Facebook may be the ‘comeback story of 2019’ as stock soars higher
text:
Facebook Inc. shares were soaring toward their best performance in three years on Thursday, after the company’s latest quarterly numbers restored confidence in the beleaguered social-media giant.
“The most draconian fears ought to begin to subside,” wrote Evercore ISI analyst Anthony DiClemente, who asked whether Facebook could emerge as tech’s “comeback story of 2019.”
Facebook FB, +11.14% shares hit an intraday high of $171.68 Thursday morning, a gain of more than 14% from Wednesday’s closing price that would add more than $60 billion to a market capitalization that had been damaged by a series of scandals. Facebook’s stock was headed for its biggest single-day increase since a 15.5% gain following fourth-quarter earnings on Jan. 28, 2016 .
Fueling excitement are the company’s better-than-feared financial disclosures released Wednesday afternoon about its core service. Daily active users climbed to 1.52 billion, up 9% from a year earlier, and Chief Financial Officer Dave Wehner said that engagement around “Facebook Blue,” the traditional site, is consistent with the user trends. That means “stability in the developed markets” and growth in developing markets, he added.
In the U.S. and Canada, Facebook’s daily-active-user count inched up to 282 million from 277 million a year earlier, while monthly active users for the region increased to 242 million from 239 million.
An erosion in core Facebook usage was “not to be observed in user metrics,” wrote Evercore’s DiClemente, helping put to bed some concerns that users were fleeing the main Facebook site in favor of platforms like Instagram, which aren’t monetized as well yet. He rates the stock at outperform with a $195 price target.
Opinion: Facebook had a bad year? Not judging by its bottom line
Needham’s Laura Martin said that the stable monthly-active-user counts for the U.S. and Canada over 2018 served as one of “the most important upside drivers,” especially given “relentless” negative headlines about the company. She has a buy rating and $170 price target on shares.
Facebook is making some progress as it tries to drive more advertiser interest in ephemeral Stories posts, though there’s still work to be done. Investors have been worried about a shift among users toward Stories consumption, since Facebook doesn’t make as much money off this type of content as it does on through its more traditional feeds.
The company said it stepped up its ad-tech efforts with Stories during the latest quarter, making it easier for marketers to convert existing “feed” ads into ones that would work on the Stories platform as well. That news was encouraging, but Wehner said that Facebook expects to see a deceleration in revenue growth in the year ahead, in part because Stories ad impressions are growing but these placements command lower rates than more traditional ones.
“From a pricing perspective, we’ve got to improve our ability to grow the number of advertisers using Stories and improve price there,” the CFO said.

Piper Jaffray analyst Michael Olson said that Facebook’s management seems “willing to take the short-term hit” that comes from lower Stories ad prices due to its long-term belief in the potential of the format. He has an overweight rating on the shares and upped his target to $195 from $190 following the report.
Facebook executives spoke about continued investments in security-related areas, following a spate of scandals around election interference, user privacy and hate speech. Total expenses in the quarter reached $9.1 billion, up 62% from a year ago, partly due to spending that aimed to improve the health of Facebook’s platform. These ongoing efforts are expected to hurt Facebook’s margins yet again, but several analysts think the company is being cautious with its expectation for mid-single-digit declines in the revenue growth rate in the first quarter relative to the fourth quarter.

Canaccord Genuity analyst Maria Ripps argued that the forecast “likely bakes in a lot of conservatism” given uncertainty about macroeconomic issues. She rates the stock a buy and upped her price target to $200 from $180.
The earnings report came as Facebook faced criticism for paying users to download a “research” app that gave the company “root” access to sensitive user data. Apple Inc. AAPL, +0.76% deemed the app a violation of its policies and revoked Facebook’s ability to issue apps that circumvent the App Store.
Of the 49 analysts tracked by FactSet who cover Facebook’s stock, 40 have buy ratings, seven have hold ratings, and two have sell ratings. The average price target is $191.58, 13% above current levels.
The stock has gained 11.6% in the past three months, while the S&P 500 SPX, +0.67% has declined 1.1%.
Emily Bary Emily Bary is a MarketWatch reporter based in New York.
